dec_unequal_places.name: Decimals With Different Numbers of Places (option)
dec_unequal_places.teaches: adding and subtracting decimals with different numbers of decimal places and with whole numbers (3.4 + 2.15; 7 − 2.36), writing placeholder zeros
dec_unequal_places.representation: the column (stack) cell with the decimal-point track; the shorter number is set in by the pupil, empty boxes show where a placeholder 0 goes; support fades from "boxes shown" to a blank grid
dec_unequal_places.why: both decimal column skills always deal equal numbers of places, so the alignment misconception is never met
dec_unequal_places.option: places "different" (1 dp with 2 dp, whole with decimal), also on sub_decimal

div_dec_2dp.option: dividend places "1 or 2" and "write a zero to finish"
div_dec_2dp.name: Divide Decimals by Integers: Hundredths (option)
div_dec_2dp.teaches: dividing decimals with up to two decimal places by a 1-digit integer with short division, including exchanging into hundredths and writing a zero to finish (3.48 ÷ 4 = 0.87; 3.5 ÷ 2 = 1.75)
div_dec_2dp.representation: one boxed cell: the short-division bus stop with the decimal point drawn and lined up in the quotient row (structural), one digit box per place; place-value headers (O . t h) over the boxes as the fading hint; write the quotient in the boxes
div_dec_2dp.why: div_decimal deals only 1-dp dividends with 1-dp quotients

expr_two_letters.option: letters "two" and values "positive whole numbers, no powers"
expr_two_letters.name: Substitute Into Two-Letter Expressions (option)
expr_two_letters.teaches: substituting two given values into an expression with two letters (a + 2b with a = 5, b = 3; 3x − y), with whole positive values and no powers (Y6 size)
expr_two_letters.representation: one boxed cell: the expression in large Andika (a + 2b), the values on a card below (a = 5, b = 3); a structural substitution line "[ ] + 2 × [ ] = [ ]" whose empty boxes the pupil fills with the values, then the result slot; the substitution line fades to the result slot only
expr_two_letters.why: evaluate_expression and evaluate_expression_hard use one letter only and mix in powers and negative values

expr_two_ops.name: Form Expressions With Two Operations (option)
expr_two_ops.teaches: forming expressions with a letter and two operations (2a + 3, 4(b − 1)) from words, a function machine or a bar model, in algebraic notation (3n, not 3 × n)
expr_two_ops.representation: a boxed cell with a drawn 2-box function machine (In → × 2 → + 3 → Out, the In is a letter) or a bar model; write the expression in the box; word bank of "add, double, times"
expr_two_ops.why: write_expression is one operation from words only
expr_two_ops.option: form "two operations" (machine, bar model, words) and notation "algebraic convention"

f_to_d_division.name: Fraction to Decimal by Division (option)
f_to_d_division.teaches: writing a fraction as a decimal (and so as a percentage) by dividing the numerator by the denominator with short division (3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 = 37.5%; 1/3 ≈ 0.333)
f_to_d_division.representation: a boxed cell holding a short-division bus stop for 3 ÷ 8 with the decimal point and placeholder zeros drawn (3.000), digit boxes for the quotient; the equation 3/8 = [ ] below
f_to_d_division.why: frac_as_division stops at a ÷ b = a/b; no skill carries the division to a decimal
f_to_d_division.option: method "by short division" (eighths, and thirds rounded to 3 dp)

f_to_d_factors.name: Fraction to Decimal: Any Factor Denominator (option)
f_to_d_factors.teaches: converting fractions whose denominators are factors of 10, 100 or 1,000 (2, 4, 5, 20, 25, 50, 8, 125) to decimals by making an equivalent tenths, hundredths or thousandths fraction, and thousandths both ways
f_to_d_factors.representation: a boxed cell: 7/20 = [ ]/100 = [ ] with an arrow over and under the fraction carrying an empty multiplier box (x [ ]); the arrow and the [ ]/100 frame are structural, the pupil writes the multiplier, the numerator and the decimal; the multiplier is printed only on model pages; fades to "7/20 = [ ]"
f_to_d_factors.why: f_to_d deals only 2, 4, 5, 10 and 100; Y6 asks 20ths, 25ths, 50ths and thousandths
f_to_d_factors.option: denominators "factors of 10, 100 and 1,000" (20, 25, 50, 8, 125); also on d_to_f to 3 dp

f_to_p_denoms.option: denominators "25 and 50", "simplify first", also on p_to_f "any whole percent"
f_to_p_denoms.name: Fractions to Percentages: Any Denominator (option)
f_to_p_denoms.teaches: converting fractions with denominators 25 and 50, and fractions that must be simplified first (9/12, 12/40), to percentages by making hundredths; and any whole percentage back to its simplest fraction (35% = 7/20)
f_to_p_denoms.representation: one boxed cell: 7/25 = [ ]/100 = [ ] % with an arrow over and under the fraction carrying an empty multiplier box (x [ ]); the [ ]/100 frame is structural, the pupil writes the multiplier, the numerator and the percent; for "simplify first" a first line 9/12 = [ ]/[ ]; the multiplier is printed only on model pages
f_to_p_denoms.why: f_to_p deals only 2, 4, 5, 10, 20 and 100; p_to_f deals only 10, 20, 25, 50 and 75%

frac_div_int_any.option: non-unit fraction / whole: numerator a multiple of the divisor (6/7 / 3 = 2/7), then any fraction via an equivalent fraction (2/3 / 4 = 8/12 / 4 = 2/12)
frac_div_int_any.name: Divide Any Fraction by an Integer (option)
frac_div_int_any.teaches: dividing a non-unit fraction by a whole number: share the numerator when it divides exactly, otherwise rename the fraction with a larger numerator first
frac_div_int_any.representation: equation cell with a fraction bar model above (structural: one bar cut into the fraction, then each part split into the divisor), answer as a stacked fraction slot; the hint step "rename first" fades
frac_div_int_any.why: div_unit_frac_nv and div_unit_fraction only divide UNIT fractions (1/3 / 2); WRM S3 and S4 divide non-unit fractions.

mean_missing.name: Find a Missing Value From the Mean (option)
mean_missing.teaches: using the mean x number of items = total to find a missing value, and the mean in a context
mean_missing.representation: a boxed list of numbers with one blank box and "mean = 6"; write the total, then the missing number
mean_missing.why: mean only asks for the mean of a list; the WRM step also finds a missing value from a given mean.

metric_decimal_convert.name: Convert Metric Measures With Decimals (option)
metric_decimal_convert.teaches: converting metric length and mass in both directions when the amount or the answer is a decimal (3.4 km = 3,400 m; 650 g = 0.65 kg)
metric_decimal_convert.representation: a boxed cell: "3.4 km = [ ] m" with the unit fact (1 km = 1,000 m) above; support: a place-value shift chart as on place_value_10x, fading to the equation only
metric_decimal_convert.why: Length and mass conversions with decimal amounts (3.4 km = □ m, 650 g = □ kg) are dealt by no skill; capacity already deals 0.25 L ↔ 250 mL.
metric_decimal_convert.option: amounts "with decimals" and direction "to the larger unit" (units Metric)

net_draw.name: Complete the Net (option)
net_draw.teaches: deciding whether a net folds into a cube or cuboid, and completing a net by adding the missing face
net_draw.representation: a net on squared paper with one face missing; shade where the face goes, or tick Yes / No for "folds into a cube"
net_draw.why: net_identify only matches a net to its solid (multiple choice); WRM also draws and checks nets.

pct_one_step.option: set "Percents" with values 50, 25, 10, 1 (and 20, 5); default 50, 25, 10, 1 for this step
pct_one_step.name: Percentage of an Amount: One Step (option)
pct_one_step.teaches: finding 50%, 25%, 10% and 1% of an amount by one division (halve, quarter, ÷ 10, ÷ 100), one percent per page first
pct_one_step.representation: one boxed cell: a B&W bar with the amount on the whole brace and "100%" under it, split into 2, 4, 10 or 100 equal parts (the split is the fading hint; the bar frame is structural); "10% of 60 = [ ]" with the answer slot; no division sign is printed, the pupil chooses it
pct_one_step.why: percent_of_number has no option to choose the percents and mixes multi-step percents (and wrong 33% items) into every page

pv10x_dp.name: Multiply and Divide Decimals by 10, 100, 1,000: Up to 3 Decimal Places (option)
pv10x_dp.teaches: multiplying and dividing numbers with 1, 2 or 3 decimal places (and decimals below 1) by 10, 100 and 1,000, writing placeholder zeros (0.307 x 1,000 = 307; 3.4 ÷ 100 = 0.034)
pv10x_dp.representation: the existing pv shift-chart cell (Th H T O . t h th, black lines, the digits drawn in the start row and empty boxes in the answer row); the arrows showing the shift are the fading hint; write the answer in the slot
pv10x_dp.why: the Decimals option deals only 1-dp numbers × a power and whole numbers ÷ a power

ratio_language.name: Ratio Language (option)
ratio_language.teaches: describing a ratio in words from a picture: "for every 2 red counters there are 3 blue counters", including the reverse sentence
ratio_language.representation: a boxed cell with a row of line-drawn counters (filled and open circles, no colour) and the sentence frame "For every [ ] ___ there are [ ] ___"; word bank for the object names; numbers only to write
ratio_language.why: WRM teaches ratio language before the colon; ratio_intro starts at the colon
ratio_language.option: variant "for every … there are …" from a picture (no colon)

reflex_angles.name: Reflex Angles (option)
reflex_angles.teaches: naming reflex angles (more than 180 degrees) alongside acute, right, obtuse and straight
reflex_angles.representation: one boxed cell: an angle drawn with the arc on the outside; tick the name (acute / obtuse / reflex) from a word bank, then write its size as 360 minus the inner angle
reflex_angles.why: identify_angles offers right, acute, obtuse and straight but not reflex, which Y6 classifies.

wp_long_div.option: multi-digit numbers: up to 4-digit / 2-digit, remainder interpreted
wp_long_div.name: Long Division Word Problems (option)
wp_long_div.teaches: division stories that need short or long division of 3-4 digit numbers by 1- or 2-digit divisors, with the remainder interpreted (round up, round down, or as a fraction)
wp_long_div.representation: word-work cell: the story in Andika, a bar model frame below (structural, stays), a working box with the long-division bracket grid, one answer slot with a unit label and a tick box: round up / round down / remainder
wp_long_div.why: div_word_problems and remainder_interpret use divisor <= 20 and dividend <= 10 x divisor; Y6 problems need long division.

wp_multidigit.name: Multi-Digit Word Problems (option)
wp_multidigit.teaches: one- and two-step multiplication stories that need a written method (1,250 seats x 24 rows)
wp_multidigit.representation: word-work cell: the story in Andika, a bar model frame below (structural, stays), a working box with the column multiplication grid, one answer slot with a unit label; no pictures in the plain variant
wp_multidigit.why: Every multiplication word problem uses fact-sized numbers; Y6 stories need long multiplication.
